abstract_sentences.text: Sparse sketches such as the sparse Johnson–Lindenstrauss transform are a core primitive in randomized numerical linear algebra because they leverage random sparsity to reduce the arithmetic cost of sketching, while still offering strong approximation guarantees.
Their random sparsity, however, is at odds with efficient implementations on modern GPUs, since it leads to irregular memory access patterns that degrade memory bandwidth utilization.

Motivated by this tension, we pursue a sketch–kernel co-design approach: we design a new family of sparse sketches, BLOCKPERM-SJLT, whose sparsity structure is chosen to enable FLASHSKETCH, a corresponding optimized CUDA kernel that implements these sketches efficiently.
The design of BLOCKPERM-SJLT introduces a tunable parameter that explicitly trades off the tension between GPU-efficiency and sketching robustness.
We provide theoretical guarantees for BLOCKPERM-SJLT under the oblivious subspace embedding (OSE) framework, and also analyze the effect of the tunable parameter on sketching quality.
We empirically evaluate FLASHSKETCH on standard RandNLA benchmarks, as well as an end-to-end ML data attribution pipeline called GraSS.

FLASHSKETCH pushes the Pareto frontier of sketching quality versus speed, across a range of regimes and tasks, and achieves a global geomean speedup of roughly 1.7× over the prior state-of-the-art GPU sketches.

method_moves.current_answer: Partition input/output coordinates into M blocks.

Every nonzero block is an independent sparse JL matrix with s nonzeros per column.

method_moves.current_answer: FlashSketch moves scatter-add into private shared memory and uses Θ(k n) global writes.

method_summary.objects: A∈R^{d×n}, S∈R^{k×d}, M, Br, Bc, κ, s, Tk, Tn, block neighborhoods N(g), and shared tiles sA/sY.
method_summary.input: Dense input matrix A and kernel tile identifiers (g,j).
method_summary.output: Y=SA, with one global output-tile write after shared-memory accumulation.
method_summary.objective: Trade sketch quality/mixing against GPU locality and memory efficiency through κ.
method_summary.assumptions: d and k are divisible by M in the exposition and are padded in practice; block-wiring permutations are edge-disjoint.

experimental_design.name: Evaluation levels
experimental_design.description: The evaluation first measures primitive sketch runtime/distortion, then standard RandNLA tasks and the GraSS data-attribution pipeline.

experimental_design.name: Timing and precision
experimental_design.description: CUDA events; mean over 10 post-warm-up iterations; FP32 for sketching and downstream tasks.

experimental_design.name: GPU hardware
experimental_design.description: Main results/table run on an NVIDIA RTX 4090; Appendix G is explicitly RTX A6000.

experimental_design.name: Baselines
experimental_design.description: Dense Gaussian/cuBLAS, sparse SJLT/cuSPARSE, SJLT/GraSS kernel, and SRHT/Dao-AILab FHT.

experimental_design.name: Inputs
experimental_design.description: Synthetic Gaussian; synthetic low-rank + noise; SuiteSparse spal_004 at about 1.4% density; GPT2-medium and Qwen2-1.5B stacked weights.

experimental_design.name: RandNLA tasks and metrics
experimental_design.description: Gram approximation, OSE, sketch-and-ridge regression, and sketch-and-solve; exact metrics are defined in Appendix F.1.

evidence.anchor: relative error in the computed Gram matrix

experimental_design.name: Parameter sweep encoding
experimental_design.description: Appendix legends map marker shapes to k and line styles/colours to methods and (κ,s) settings.

evidence.anchor: Marker shapes indicate sketch dimension k

experimental_design.name: GraSS treatment control
experimental_design.description: Only GraSS's SJLT projection kernel is replaced; all other pipeline components and LDS evaluation code path remain identical.

evidence.anchor: keeping all other pipeline components fixed

experimental_design.name: LDS denominator and aggregation
experimental_design.description: For each z, Spearman correlation is over m=50 retrained 50%-subsampled training sets; reported LDS averages over evaluation examples.

experimental_design.name: Random seeds
experimental_design.description: The PDF names 10 timing iterations but provides no random-seed count or seed values for the sketch/benchmark experiments.

experimental_design.name: Hyperparameter budget
experimental_design.description: The kernel uses a small menu of templates, yet the exact menu and an exhaustive tuning budget are not given; Appendix B calls the procedure non-exhaustive.

experimental_design.name: Data leakage controls
experimental_design.description: No standalone leakage-control protocol is stated; GraSS describes train-subset retraining but no cross-dataset leakage analysis.

result_inventory.claim: FlashSketch has a 1.73× global geomean speedup versus the next-best baseline over the listed RandNLA aggregate.
result_inventory.value: 1.73× global geomean; abstract rounds this to roughly 1.7×.
result_inventory.comparison: Table 1 aggregates shapes, datasets and configs over four RandNLA tasks against four dense/sparse baselines.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Geometric mean of speedups; the table does not specify configuration weights or an uncertainty interval.

evidence.anchor: Global geomean vs next best baseline: 1.73x

result_inventory.claim: Primitive Gram/OSE speedups are largest against the FHT baseline in the aggregate table.
result_inventory.comparison: Dense Gaussian/cuBLAS, SJLT/cuSPARSE, SJLT/GraSS, and SRHT/FHT.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Task-level geomean speedups in Table 1; quality is separately plotted as error–time Pareto frontiers.

result_inventory.claim: End-to-end sketch-and-ridge and sketch-and-solve retain aggregate speedups.
result_inventory.comparison: Four baseline columns; residual quality is visualized against total wall-clock time in F.4–F.5 and G.3–G.4.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Geomean speedups in Table 1 plus configuration-level Pareto panels; no test or interval reported.

result_inventory.claim: Replacing only the GraSS projection kernel can reach about 3.2× speedup while retaining LDS on the plotted MNIST setting.
result_inventory.value: up to ∼3.2×; k=1024, 2048, 4096 after sketching from dimension 4k.
result_inventory.comparison: FlashSketch versus GraSS and three other projection baselines on an MLP trained on MNIST.
result_inventory.statistical_method: LDS is an average of per-example Spearman correlations over 50 retraining subsets; Figure 4 plots LDS against projection time per sample.

statistical_analysis.central_tendency: Mean of 10 post-warm-up CUDA-event iterations; global/task geomean speedups; average LDS over evaluation examples.
statistical_analysis.dispersion_or_intervals: not_present for timing/configuration uncertainty; no confidence intervals or error-definition text accompanies the main results.
statistical_analysis.figure_caption_independence: Main Figures 1, 3, 4 and Table 1 state axes/task/hardware; the F/G panel captions rely on Figures 5–6 for the method/parameter legend.

ablation_inventory.description: The panels cover synthetic Gaussian, low-rank + noise, GPT2/Qwen2 weights and SuiteSparse across d=16,384 through 262,144 and n=512/1,024.

claim_closure.claim: B LOCK P ERM-SJLT jointly provides block locality and mixing.
claim_closure.method_response: Section 4 gives edge-disjoint κ-regular block wiring and intra-block SJLT mixing.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 2 visualizes the structure; F/G sweep κ,s in task-level Pareto panels.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: No conclusion section; Section 8 keeps the κ tradeoff as an explicit scope condition.

evidence.anchor: preserves block locality while improving mixing

claim_closure.claim: The co-designed kernel avoids global atomics and improves realized speed.
claim_closure.method_response: Algorithm 1 makes sY private to a thread block and writes it globally once; Section 5.3 contrasts Θ(sdn) global atomics with Θ(kn) global writes.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 1/3, Table 1 and F/G provide quality–speed outcomes.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 8 narrows the claim for low occupancy and large κ.

evidence.anchor: single global write per output tile

claim_closure.claim: Increasing κ improves robustness through neighborhood-coherence smoothing.
claim_closure.method_response: Definition 6.1/Equation (4) defines µ_nbr; Theorem 6.2 and Equation (8) give OSE and smoothing relations.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix F/G expose multiple κ,s curves, but do not isolate the theoretical distributional assumption.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 8 and Remark A.12 identify the independent-permutation versus structured-distinct implementation mismatch.

claim_closure.claim: FlashSketch improves the Pareto frontier by about 1.7× over prior GPU sketches across tasks.
claim_closure.method_response: The kernel construction is the proposed cause; there is no speed theorem.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1 reports 1.73× global geomean and F/G supply configuration panels on two GPUs.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: No conclusion section; Section 8 limits the speed regime and κ range.

claim_closure.claim: Replacing GraSS's projection kernel retains attribution quality while accelerating projection.
claim_closure.method_response: Section 7.4 fixes all pipeline components other than the SJLT projection kernel; Appendix E defines LDS.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 4 gives MNIST LDS–time Pareto and up to ∼3.2× speedup.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 8 identifies the need to connect OSE to broader downstream learning performance.

limitations.name: Low-k occupancy
limitations.description: FlashSketch is most advantageous when A is dense and k≪d but large enough to saturate the GPU; low k limits speedups.

limitations.name: Large-κ input-read cost
limitations.description: Very large κ increases input reads and can limit speedups.

limitations.name: κ selection is empirical
limitations.description: The paper empirically chooses the Pareto-optimal κ and leaves an adaptive choice for future work.

limitations.name: Theory/implementation permutation mismatch
limitations.description: Theory assumes independent uniform permutations, while the kernel samples edge-disjoint distinct structured permutations with dependence between neighborhoods.

limitations.name: OSE scope
limitations.description: The authors do not prove direct guarantees for their Gram-matrix metric or downstream learning performance.

limitations.name: Statistical uncertainty reporting
limitations.description: The PDF reports timing means, geomeans, and LDS averages but no confidence interval, hypothesis test, multiple-comparison procedure, or random-seed count.

measurement_disagreements.description: No automatic measurement draft was supplied for this reading. Page ranges, figure/table/algorithm inventory, and formula counts were determined from the verified PDF directly.

final_judgment.single_storyline: 将 sparse-sketch 随机性组织成 edge-disjoint block permutations，使 CUDA thread block 能私有累积一个 output tile；κ 同时调节 GPU locality、mixing 和由 µ_nbr 表示的 OSE 条件。
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: 张力、block construction、Algorithm 1、µ_nbr/ Theorem 6.2、baseline/task design、Table 1、Figures 1/3/4、GraSS control 与限制段落。
final_judgment.appendix_moves: A 放证明，B–D 放 kernel/alternative/wiring，E 放 GraSS-LDS 细节，F–G 放 128 张配置级 ablation 图；主文可理解机制和聚合结论，细粒度稳健性依赖附录。
final_judgment.best_pattern: 引言先用一个 Pareto preview 具体化张力，再以 construction → kernel → coherence → benchmark 的四项贡献和一张 task×baseline 表串起论证。
final_judgment.largest_gap: 理论的 independent-uniform permutation 模型与 structured edge-disjoint runtime wiring 不同；速度机制未做逐组件隔离，主结果也未报告 timing/seed uncertainty。
final_judgment.transfer_rule: 在随机算法遇到硬件 memory/synchronization 瓶颈时，先寻找可证明的结构化随机中介量，再让 data structure、kernel 与 evaluation 围绕它共同设计。
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: 仅当结构仍保留任务关键的混合性质、硬件瓶颈已被明确定位、且理论与实现分布之间的近似条件可陈述并可实测时适用。
